text:
maria: Kickoff: drafting a benchmark narrative for an upcoming launch. Deliverables: one short blog post, a one-page PDF, three reproducible charts (hero + two deep dives), a 30-min webinar focused on operators, and clear inbound routing so only high-intent leads get AE/SE outreach. Need quick takes on chart specs, three distinct hooks, microcopy variants, and routing signals.

sam: Love the pragmatic focus. Proposed hooks: 1) token economics (USD per 1k tokens for common tasks), 2) operational risk (p50 vs p99 and how caching changes the tail), 3) ROI by workload (cost-per-response for chat vs summarization at different batch sizes).

maria: Hero chart idea: compact scatter where x = cost per 1k tokens (USD), y = median latency (ms), and marker size = throughput (responses/sec). Color by config (redwood-optimized, open-default, hosted-generic). That packs three signals into one glance. Caption must call out assumptions (model family, hardware equivalence, avg prompt length).

abby: For deep dives: (A) Tail latency waterfall: percentile (x) vs latency (y) lines for Redwood vs baseline, shaded p95-p99 bands; (B) Batch economics: grouped bars by batch size showing cost per 1k responses and latency overlay as a thin line. Add small table of key parameters in the PDF footer.

leo: Routing rules (practical):
- signal: benchmark_pdf_downloaded == true -> route to AE+SE (priority HIGH)
- signal: webinar_attended == true AND company_size >= 200 -> AE outreach (priority HIGH)
- signal: sign_up_for_run_slice == true AND domain_verified == true -> SE follow-up (priority MED)
- otherwise -> nurture (product emails + quickstart)
Also add a hidden field on the signup form: primary_use_case (choices: chat, search, summarization, code).

zach: Microcopy candidates for A/B tests (hero + CTA):
A) "See the token math: faster responses, smarter spend."
B) "Benchmark your slice: cost, latency, and throughput in minutes."
C) "Keep latency. Lose cost. Run your slice on Redwood."
I prefer B for the modal (actionable) and C for heavier enterprise CTAs.

maria: Chart spec YAML (for design/dev):
```yaml
- id: hero_scatter_econ
  type: scatter
  x: cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
  y: median_latency_ms
  size: throughput_rps
  series: [redwood_optimized, open_default, hosted_generic]
  callouts: [chat_512_tokens, long_context_2048]
  assumptions: [hardware=A100_equiv, model_family=llama2_like, avg_prompt=120_tokens]
- id: tail_waterfall
  type: line_area
  x: percentile
  y: latency_ms
  series: [redwood, baseline]
  annotations: [p95_gap, p99_gap]
  note: include simulated outage buffer overlay
- id: batch_economics
  type: grouped_bar_with_line
  x: batch_size
  bars: cost_per_1000_responses
  line: median_latency_ms
  series: [batch_1, batch_8, batch_32]
  footnote: show input prompt lengths and memory settings
```

maria: Tone and claim guidance: be conservative and verifiable. Use conditional language like: "In our testbed, enabling batch+cache reduced per-response cost up to 4x; many slices saw 1.5x-2.5x improvements." Link full methodology in the PDF and blog.

sam: Webinar run-of-show (30m): 6m headline findings + key chart walkthrough, 12m live demo (copy-paste eval kit: run slice, toggle batch/cache, view results), 8m customer Q&A + CTA to run-a-slice trial + office hours sign-up. Demo MUST include commands and the exact eval script path.

abby: For the one-pager PDF outline:
- page1: hero claim + hero scatter + 2-sentence methodology
- page2: tail waterfall chart + short takeaways
- page3: batch economics chart + practical knobs (batching, prefix cache, quant) with code snippets
- footer: hardware & prompt assumptions, link to eval repo, contact CTA

maria: CTA phrasing experiments: "Run your slice on Redwood Dedicated" vs "Get a free eval run". Track conversion to AE contact and demo requests.

leo: I'll produce a small routing JSON sample and map the three product events to customer.io triggers by tomorrow morning. I'll also add the primary_use_case field on the form.

zach: I'll set up the microcopy A/B in the modal and measure CTR -> signup -> run-slice funnel. Aim to have tests live with initial traffic by launch day.

maria: Action items + owners (deadline: draft by Fri EOD):
- blog lead (2 short paragraphs) + methodology blurb (maria + sam)
- hero + deep-dive chart mocks (SVGs) (sam + abby)
- one-pager PDF outline & snippets (maria)
- routing JSON sample + event map (leo)
- microcopy A/B and modal config (zach)
- webinar run-of-show + demo script (sam)

marketing-bot: Webinar calendar created: https://cal.link/redwood-bench-ops  slots: Mon 11am / Wed 4pm / Fri 10am.

maria: Great. Keep claims reproducible and avoid bold multipliers in headlines. We'll iterate on copy after early CTR signals. Ping here if blocked. :rocket:
